form.label: Exposure
form.description: Which open findings the network can actually reach, and which of them sit inside containers.

search.query: | `riskability_reachability_for("*", $conf_tok|s$)` | search (hostname=$host_tok$) | search $reach_filter$ $exploit_filter$ | eval rk_reach = if(reach_rank >= 2, 1, 0), rk_local = if(reach_rank == 1, 1, 0), rk_unknown = if(reach_rank < 0, 1, 0), rk_kev_reach = if(reach_rank >= 2 AND is_kev == 1, 1, 0) | stats sum(rk_kev_reach) AS kev_reachable, sum(rk_reach) AS reachable, sum(rk_local) AS local_only, sum(rk_unknown) AS unassessed, count AS findings, dc(package) AS packages BY hostname | eventstats dc(hostname) AS fleet_hosts, sum(reachable) AS fleet_reachable | eval shown_hosts = min(10, fleet_hosts) | sort 50000 - kev_reachable, - reachable, - findings

div.b: Reachability re-orders work. It does not remove any.
div.span: Every finding here is still a real vulnerability. This page adds what EPSS and the KEV catalogue cannot: whether this copy answers the network. A package with no listening port is not safe - it is reached by something other than a socket, or by an attacker already inside - but it is not tonight's fix. Nothing is ever coloured green, because nothing here is finished. Read a quiet row as "later", never as "no".

Defaults to all matches, not high confidence only. What listens on a port is usually a compiled binary, this app's least confident match: it can tell a Go executable is serving without knowing which module versions are inside. Filtering those out would empty the reachable rows, so they are shown and labelled instead. Check the Confidence column before acting on one.

panel.title: What to do first - open findings by reach and by exploit likelihood

search.query: | `riskability_reachability_for("*", $conf_tok|s$)` | search (hostname=$host_tok$) | stats count AS findings BY exploit_class, reach_class, tier | fields exploit_class, reach_class, findings, tier

viz.option: Nothing to place. Either no open findings match this host filter, or the exposure snapshot has not run yet - see the assessment coverage panel below.

div.span: Two known-exploited findings on a wildcard port make the darkest cell; sixteen thousand unreachable ones make the coolest. Empty cells are drawn rather than omitted, so a row reading zero across is unambiguous. The dashed row is not assessed: unranked because the collector on that host never reported its listening ports. Treat it as unknown risk, not low risk.

search.query: | head 10 | table hostname, kev_reachable, reachable, local_only, unassessed, findings | rename hostname AS "Host", kev_reachable AS "Known-exploited and reachable", reachable AS "Reachable findings", local_only AS "Loopback only", unassessed AS "Not assessed", findings AS "Open findings"

viz.option: No host has an open finding at this filter.

div.b: Showing $shown_hosts$ of $fleet_hosts$ hosts with findings, worst first.
div.span: The matrix above is fleet-wide and holds thirty cells whatever the input. This list grows a row per machine, so it is cut to ten and the number it was cut from is printed above. Order is known-exploited-and-reachable, then reachable, then open findings: one exploited CVE answering the internet outranks a thousand findings nothing can get to. $fleet_reachable$ findings across the fleet answer a network address.

Click a row to point the chain below at that host and narrow the detail table to it. With nothing selected the chain follows the top row, so it is not empty on load. Selecting a matrix cell narrows this list to the machines that have those findings. For the rest, sort or filter this page by host, or use Hosts, one machine at a time.
Click a matrix cell, chain node or container row to narrow the detail table at the bottom of this page.
Page narrowed. The matrix and the ranked host list stay whole so you can pick something else. Clear also closes the container detail panel if one is open.
Filtered by $drill_note$

panel.title: How the network gets there - port, process, container, package, CVE

search.query: | `riskability_reachability_for("*", $conf_tok|s$)` | search (hostname=$host_tok$) | search $chain_filter$ | search $reach_filter$ $exploit_filter$ | where reach_rank >= 1 AND isnotnull(chain_text) AND chain_text != "" | eventstats dc(cve_id) AS rk_host_cves BY hostname | sort 200000 - rk_host_cves, hostname | streamstats dc(hostname) AS rk_host_rank | where rk_host_rank <= 3 | `riskability_chain_hops` | eventstats dc(hostname) AS rk_drawn | eval source = if(rk_drawn > 1 AND source_kind IN ("edge", "listener", "listener-unknown", "container"), source . " @" . hostname, source) | eval target = if(rk_drawn > 1 AND target_kind IN ("edge", "listener", "listener-unknown", "container"), target . " @" . hostname, target) | eventstats dc(cve_id) AS rk_port_cves BY hostname, n_edge | sort 200000 hostname, - rk_port_cves, n_edge | streamstats dc(n_edge) AS rk_port_rank BY hostname | where rk_port_rank <= 10 | eval rk_epss = coalesce(epss, 0) | stats max(rk_epss) AS rk_epss, max(is_kev) AS rk_kev, dc(cve_id) AS cves BY source, source_kind, target, target_kind | eval rk_kev = coalesce(rk_kev, 0) | eval rk_cve = if(target_kind=="cve" OR target_kind=="cve-kev", 1, 0) | sort 20000 source, - rk_kev, - rk_epss | streamstats count AS rk_rank BY source, rk_cve | eval rk_drop = if(rk_cve==1 AND rk_kev!=1 AND rk_rank > 3, 1, 0) | eventstats sum(rk_drop) AS rk_hidden BY source | eval rk_drop = if(rk_hidden == 1, 0, rk_drop), rk_hidden = if(rk_hidden == 1, 0, rk_hidden) | where rk_drop = 0 | appendpipe [ stats max(rk_hidden) AS n BY source, source_kind | where n > 0 | eval target = n . " more in " . source, target_kind = "cve", cves = n ] | sort 5000 - cves | head 160 | fields source, source_kind, target, target_kind, cves

viz.option: No chain to draw. Three causes look identical here: these hosts may have nothing behind a listening port; the selected matrix cell may be an unreachable row, which by definition has no route, so the empty panel is the answer; or these hosts may have none of the findings in that cell, in which case the ranked list above says which hosts do. Check the assessment coverage panel below to confirm their ports were measured at all.

div.b: The chain draws at most three hosts at once.
div.span: A chain is a route through one machine; across a fleet it would merge every copy of sshd into one node and sum edge widths over unrelated machines. Only the three most exposed hosts of the current selection are drawn, and when more than one is drawn every port, process and container carries its machine, so two hosts running the same service never merge into one node claiming a route neither has. Packages and CVEs stay shared: three machines converging on one vulnerable library is worth seeing. Ten hosts would be about 120 CVE nodes in a column 620 pixels tall, five pixels a node; the two hosts here come to 24.

Pick hosts at the top of the page, or click a row in the ranked list to aim the chain at one machine without collapsing that list. Selecting a matrix cell narrows the chain to those findings; selecting an unreachable row empties it, correctly - those findings have no route.

Ten listening ports per host, 160 hops in total. The busiest are kept, and the cut is by port, so a dropped port takes its whole route with it. On the fleet this was built against, one host's chain comes to nine CVE nodes and the other's to fifteen; the cap is for a machine running thirty services, not for these.

Every hop is measured, and the picture is still not the whole route. The collector saw the port, the process holding it and the packages inside; not your firewall, reverse proxy or network segmentation. A wildcard bind means the process would answer any address that reaches the host, not that the internet can reach it. Bubble size is the largest number of CVEs reachable through any single hop touching that node, so sibling sizes do not add up. A dashed node is a hole in what the collector could see - a port answering with no process attributed to it - not a hop known to be harmless. Ports with no package behind them never reach this graph, since nothing can be matched against them; they are counted in Ports with no package below. Each package names its known-exploited CVEs and its three highest-scoring others; the rest roll up into one "N more in <package>" node, unless that would hold a single CVE, which is named instead. Nodes are labelled where there is height for it; in a dense column the busiest keep their labels and the rest can be read by hovering.

search.query: | `riskability_hosts_seen` | search (hostname=$host_tok$) | lookup riskability_exposure_hoststate_lookup hostname OUTPUT listeners, wildcard_listeners, unattributed_listeners, os_listeners, packages_behind_ports, containers, assessed_at | eval status = if(isnull(assessed_at), "never reported a listening port", "assessed") | eval assessed = if(isnull(assessed_at), "never", strftime(assessed_at, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M")) | eval listeners = coalesce(listeners, 0), wildcard_listeners = coalesce(wildcard_listeners, 0), unattributed_listeners = coalesce(unattributed_listeners, 0), os_listeners = coalesce(os_listeners, 0), packages_behind_ports = coalesce(packages_behind_ports, 0), containers = coalesce(containers, 0) | table hostname, status, assessed, listeners, wildcard_listeners, os_listeners, unattributed_listeners, packages_behind_ports, containers | sort 5000 status, - wildcard_listeners | rename hostname AS "Host", status AS "Exposure", assessed AS "Measured at", listeners AS "Ports", wildcard_listeners AS "Any-address ports", os_listeners AS "Held by the OS", unattributed_listeners AS "Ports with no package", packages_behind_ports AS "Packages", containers AS "Containers behind ports"

viz.option: No hosts have reported inventory yet.

div.b: A host that never reported ports is not a host with no ports.
div.span: Older collectors report inventory but no exposure. Their findings land in the not assessed row of the matrix rather than the calm one, so a fleet does not look safer for being less well instrumented. "Held by the OS" and "Ports with no package" are two further gaps, and not the same one: the first is a port answered by the operating system itself - Windows System and svchost - visible but not assessable against a package feed. The second is a port the app could not identify at all.

panel.title: Which open findings are on a library something actually loads

search.query: | `riskability_open_findings` | search (hostname=$host_tok$) | `riskability_load_evidence` | eval pressure = case( isnotnull(kev_added) AND kev_added != "", "known exploited", isnotnull(epss) AND epss >= 0.1, "high EPSS", 1=1, "neither") | stats count AS value BY load_class, load_rank, pressure | sort - load_rank | eval category = load_class, series = pressure | table category, series, value

div.b: Read the bottom two bars before the top one.
div.span: Not assessed is not a small bar to be pleased about: it counts findings on hosts that sent no link data at all, which is every Windows host and every collector older than swinv 1.11. Not a linked library counts npm, PyPI and Go findings that no ELF link could ever describe. Neither means "nothing loads it", and a fleet where those two dominate has not been measured rather than found clean. The bar worth acting on is the top one, and the colours say whether those are also the findings the world is exploiting.

panel.title: Open findings on a library a listening process loads

search.query: | `riskability_open_findings` | search (hostname=$host_tok$) | `riskability_load_evidence` | where loaded_listening = 1 | eval sev = coalesce(severity, "not stated") | eval kev = if(isnotnull(kev_added) AND kev_added != "", "yes", "") | eval epss_pc = if(isnotnull(epss), round(epss * 100, 1), null()) | sort 500 - kev, - epss, - cvss_score | table hostname, package, installed_version, cve_id, sev, cvss_score, epss_pc, kev, loaders, loader_count | rename hostname AS "Host", package AS "Package", installed_version AS "Installed", cve_id AS "CVE", sev AS "Severity", cvss_score AS "CVSS", epss_pc AS "EPSS %", kev AS "Known exploited", loaders AS "Loaded by", loader_count AS "Loaders"

viz.option: No open finding here is on a library that a listening process loads. That is not the same as nothing being exposed: see whether these hosts were assessed at all, below.

div.b: Loading a library is not proof the vulnerable code runs.
div.span: swinv reads each binary's DT_NEEDED table without executing anything, so this says the process maps the library, not that it reaches the affected function. Most CVEs live in internal code that appears in no import table. Read it as a reason to look first, not as a verdict. The reverse is weaker still: a library arriving through dlopen, which is how nginx modules, Python extensions, PAM and NSS load, is invisible here, so an absent row is not evidence the library is unused.

panel.title: Was anything measured about what these hosts load?

search.query: | `riskability_hosts_seen` | search (hostname=$host_tok$) | lookup riskability_links_hoststate_lookup hostname OUTPUT link_rows, linked_packages, listening_loaders, unowned_libraries, assessed_at | eval status = if(isnull(assessed_at), "no link data from this host", "assessed") | eval assessed = if(isnull(assessed_at), "never", strftime(assessed_at, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M")) | eval link_rows = coalesce(link_rows, 0), linked_packages = coalesce(linked_packages, 0), listening_loaders = coalesce(listening_loaders, 0), unowned_libraries = coalesce(unowned_libraries, 0) | table hostname, status, assessed, link_rows, linked_packages, listening_loaders, unowned_libraries | sort 5000 status, - unowned_libraries | rename hostname AS "Host", status AS "Library loads", assessed AS "Measured at", link_rows AS "Links seen", linked_packages AS "Packages loaded", listening_loaders AS "Listening binaries", unowned_libraries AS "Libraries no package owns"

viz.option: No hosts have reported inventory yet.

div.b: A host with no link data is not a host that loads nothing.
div.span: Link records are read from ELF binaries, so a Windows host has none and neither does a collector older than swinv 1.11 or one run without --ndjson-include links. Those findings say not assessed rather than not seen in the load list, so a host does not look calmer for having been measured less. "Libraries no package owns" counts files that were loaded and that nothing installed provides: vendored or hand-copied libraries, which no package feed can ever match and which no version comparison will ever flag.

panel.title: Containers - a stopped container is not a safe container

search.query: | `riskability_container_findings_for("*")` | search (hostname=$host_tok$) | stats dc(cve_id) AS cves, count AS findings, dc(package) AS packages, max(epss) AS peak_epss, sum(if(isnotnull(kev_added) AND kev_added!="", 1, 0)) AS kev BY hostname, container_label, image_label, state, published, ctr_tier | eval peak_epss = round(peak_epss, 4) | sort 5000 ctr_tier, - kev, - cves | table ctr_tier, hostname, container_label, image_label, state, published, cves, kev, packages, peak_epss | rename ctr_tier AS "Priority", hostname AS "Host", container_label AS "Container", image_label AS "Image", state AS "State", published AS "Ports", cves AS "CVEs", kev AS "Known-exploited", packages AS "Packages", peak_epss AS "Peak EPSS"

viz.option: No open finding is scoped to a container. Either no containers were reported, or their images carry no matched vulnerability.

div.span: A stopped container is one docker start away from running, and its vulnerabilities are latent rather than absent. It is ranked last, not removed. A container with no published port ranks below one that publishes: the image is identical, the reach is not.
Showing container $ctr_tok$

search.query: | `riskability_container_findings_for($ctr_host_tok|s$)` | search container_label=$ctr_tok|s$ | eval kev = if(isnotnull(kev_added) AND kev_added!="", "yes", "") | eval epss = round(epss, 4) | table cve_id, package, last_version, fixed_version, severity, kev, epss, image_label, state, published | sort 5000 - epss | head 2000 | rename cve_id AS "CVE", package AS "Package", last_version AS "Installed", fixed_version AS "Fixed in", severity AS "Severity", kev AS "Known-exploited", epss AS "EPSS", image_label AS "Image", state AS "State", published AS "Ports"

div.b: These findings are the image's, not the host's.
div.span: Opened by clicking a container above. Close this panel resets the page filters as well as closing it.

They were matched against the operating system declared inside the container, often a different distribution from the host it runs on. Fixing them means rebuilding or replacing the image - patching the host will not move them.

search.query: | `riskability_reachability_for("*", $conf_tok|s$)` | search (hostname=$host_tok$) | search $reach_filter$ $exploit_filter$ $host_focus_filter$ | eval rk_nodes = mvappend(package, cve_id, split(coalesce(ports_text, ""), ", "), split(coalesce(listener_text, ""), ", "), split(coalesce(container_text, ""), ", ")) | search $node_filter$ | eval kev = if(isnotnull(kev_added) AND kev_added!="", "yes", "") | eval epss = round(epss, 4) | eval root = if(scope_id!="", scope_id, "host") | `riskability_load_evidence` | table tier, reach_class, exploit_class, load_class, confidence, cve_id, package, last_version, fixed_version, hostname, root, ports_text, listener_text, listener_path_text, container_text, loaders, kev, epss | sort 50000 - epss | head 2000 | rename tier AS "Priority", reach_class AS "Reach", exploit_class AS "Exploit likelihood", confidence AS "Confidence", cve_id AS "CVE", package AS "Package", last_version AS "Installed", fixed_version AS "Fixed in", hostname AS "Host", root AS "Root", ports_text AS "Listening on", listener_text AS "Held by", listener_path_text AS "Executable", container_text AS "Container", load_class AS "Library load", loaders AS "Loaded by", kev AS "Known-exploited", epss AS "EPSS"

div.b: Capped at 2,000 rows, highest EPSS first.
div.span: For reading a selection, not for exporting a fleet. Narrow it with the matrix or the chain above, or use Findings for the full register. "Held by" is the systemd unit or the executable's name; the full path is in its own column. "Library load" says whether a process on this host maps the package's library, read from the binary rather than from the port. Not assessed means no link data arrived, which is not the same as nothing loading it, and not a linked library marks the npm, PyPI and Go findings that no ELF link could ever describe.
